data.interpretation: The main goal is the town-wide count of orders delivered within the promised pickup and delivery times, so on_time_deliveries is the primary metric. The KPI also allows the promised times in DELIVERY_SLA to be revised. Those are contract changes, so a human must decide them. Changing the promise also changes what counts as 'on time', so loosening it can raise on_time_deliveries without customers being served any faster. Customer impact therefore has to be measured with metrics that do not depend on the promise: wait time from order to delivery (p95_wait_s, max_wait_s) and orders left undelivered (unfinished). The KPI states no numeric levels, so no targets or guard values are set.

options.label: On-time count as primary, with promise-independent customer metrics monitored

goals.text: Maximize the number of orders delivered within the promised times across the town.
Monitor the 95th-percentile order-to-delivery wait so that promise revisions do not hide slower service.
Monitor the longest order-to-delivery wait, to measure the worst customer outcome.
Monitor orders still undelivered at the end of the period.

options.note: Improvement is measured by on_time_deliveries. Any DELIVERY_SLA revision goes to a human, together with the measured change in p95_wait_s, max_wait_s and unfinished on the same seeds. This gives the reason the KPI requires before accepting a change that is worse for customers.

options.label: Literal reading: on-time count with late and unfinished orders monitored

goals.text: Maximize the number of orders delivered within the promised times across the town.
Monitor orders delivered after the promised time.
Monitor orders still undelivered at the end of the period.

options.note: Simplest reading. However, late_deliveries and on_time_deliveries both depend on the promised times. A looser promise would look like an improvement on every goal here even if customers wait longer.

options.label: Actual customer wait as primary, on-time count monitored

goals.text: Reduce the 95th-percentile order-to-delivery wait, which does not depend on the promised times.
Monitor the number of orders delivered within the promised times.
Monitor orders still undelivered at the end of the period.

options.note: Keeps the primary metric comparable across promise revisions. It departs from the KPI's stated objective (count of on-time orders), so it fits only if customer experience matters more than the promise count.

concerns: on_time_deliveries is defined relative to DELIVERY_SLA. Revising the promised times changes what counts as on time, so the count could rise from looser promises rather than faster service. Wait-time metrics are needed to measure the real effect on customers.
The KPI gives no numeric levels (no target count, rate, or maximum acceptable wait), so no targets or guard values have been set. If a floor on customer wait is intended, please state it.

The KPI is town-wide. Maximizing the total could let one company's on-time rate fall. Company-level metrics (min_company_on_time_rate, on_time_rate_gap) are not included because the KPI does not mention them.
